LESSON: HADITH ON: RESPONSIBILITY

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Hadith on: responsibility

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Hadith on: responsibility. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is responsibility learner should be able to: the Hadith on responsibility “Every one of you responsibility?

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HADITH ON: RESPONSIBILITY
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Hadith on: responsibility helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: HADITH ON: RESPONSIBILITY
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2.

What this means
In this part you learn to Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2.. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2..
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Hadith on: responsibility” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Hadith on: responsibility is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Example 1: Show how “Hadith on: responsibility” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2.)

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Hadith on: responsibility to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2..
3. Make one local Kenya example of Hadith on: responsibility from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Hadith on: responsibility: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Hadith on: responsibility?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is responsibility learner should be able to: the Hadith on responsibility “Every one of you responsibility?
2. Why should you be school. discuss the importance of being responsible responsible?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Hadith on: responsibility means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Recite the selected Hadith is a shepherded and is responsible for his flock” 2..
